summary: Eisenkot holds President Herzog's mandate until Dec 6 (extendable by up to 14 days), and his bloc, with Arab MKs' votes, has begun taking control of Knesset posts; a vote to replace Speaker Ohana with Matan Kahana is set for Nov 17. A senior UTJ rabbi has reportedly authorized talks with Eisenkot's bloc, whose preferred path, Ynet reports, is UTJ joining first with Shas or Likud defectors added later, while Agudat Yisrael's rabbinic advisers reportedly want a signed pledge on a draft-exemption law; both sides say no formal negotiations are underway. Eisenkot says talks with his partners are progressing and, per Ynet's unnamed sources, has told his team to resume contacts with Likud next week. Netanyahu says unity is still possible under his leadership and is reported to be lobbying Haredi rabbis against joining Eisenkot, while Shas says it still backs him. Joint List leader Jabareen has meanwhile listed his party's demands for cooperating with Eisenkot's bloc.

phase.now: Eisenkot has the mandate (deadline Dec 6, 2026, extendable by up to 14 days)
phase.next: If Eisenkot fails, Herzog can task another MK, who would get 28 days with no extension. The Jerusalem Post reports the change bloc is expected to replace Speaker Ohana on Tuesday, Nov 17, after electing Folkman Arrangements Committee chair.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu's Right-Religious Bloc
scenarios.note: His existing partners. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he wants Shas, Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism in any future government and that the public does not want one dependent on Ra'am and the Joint List. Without a majority, he needs defectors or a new partner from the other side. On Nov 5 UTJ declined to recommend any candidate, leaving Netanyahu without its endorsements, while Otzma Yehudit recommended him. Likud's delegation, last to meet Herzog, urged him to give Netanyahu the mandate, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 7 Herzog chose Eisenkot rather than Netanyahu to try first to form a government, Al Jazeera reports. Channel 12 reports Netanyahu tried to reach senior UTJ rabbis to have the party vote against an Eisenkot government, but was rebuffed, the Times of Israel reports. Ynet reports that an attempt by Netanyahu's associates to arrange a call with UTJ's Rabbi Dov Landau failed. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 13, citing an unnamed source, that Netanyahu is personally calling rabbis and sending emissaries to warn the Haredi parties off Eisenkot's bloc.

blockers.text: Liberman urged Likud MKs to revolt against Netanyahu and says he won't sit with him.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Arab Parties
scenarios.note: Championed by Yair Golan, who met Lapid and then Abbas on Oct 29; the Times of Israel says he is the only Jewish-led bloc leader openly backing a coalition with Ra'am. Without Yisrael Beiteinu it falls short, and analysts told JTA the public is not ready for it. Channel 12 reports Abbas himself privately called an Eisenkot minority government with outside Arab support weak or impossible. AFP reports Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition relying on Arab parties, and the Joint List's Jabareen says he would back him from outside. A senior Joint List official told Walla on Nov 1 that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Eisenkot to the president. Ynet reports Joint List and Ra'am leaders met in Nazareth on Nov 2 and will coordinate their recommendations. Ynet reports Bennett sides with Liberman against a government relying on Arab parties, believing it would collapse. On Nov 3 Golan met Joint List leaders and they agreed to keep coordinating, while the Times of Israel notes the bloc's joint statement gave no indication of how it would govern without Arab parties. On Nov 4 Ra'am announced it will recommend Eisenkot, while Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog a government cannot be formed with Arab parties. On Nov 5 the Joint List said it will recommend Eisenkot but will not formally join his coalition, offering possible outside support, Al Jazeera and ANI report. A Times of Israel analysis notes the Joint List has not said it will back an Eisenkot-led government. Eisenkot formally received the mandate on Nov 8, and the Jerusalem Post notes the Arab parties' recommendations do not commit them to joining his coalition. On Nov 8 Liberman reiterated he will not support a government dependent on Arab parties, Ynet reports. At the Nov 10 session, Ben-Gvir and other MKs heckled the Eisenkot bloc over Arab lawmakers' absence during the anthem, and Liberman posted asking whether these were the people the bloc wanted to govern with, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 11 the bloc and the Arab MKs jointly voted to elect Yashar!'s Folkman as Arrangements Committee chair, and the Joint List accused Netanyahu's Knesset speech of racism, the Jerusalem Post reports. Middle East Monitor reports Golan said on Nov 11 that a government could be formed within three weeks with Ra'am and Joint List support. On Nov 11 the Arrangements Committee voted 13–9 to recommend Liberman as chair of the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 13 Joint List leader Jabareen listed demands for cooperating with Eisenkot's bloc, including repealing the Kaminitz Law and Arab-community crime and economic plans, which the Jerusalem Post describes as hinting at informal negotiations.

Eisenkot pledged a 'Zionist government' and has not backed the idea.
Ben-Gvir urged the Shin Bet to arrest Arab party leaders if there are legal grounds over alleged Qatari funding.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Ra'am Only
scenarios.note: The 2021 Bennett–Lapid model. Ynet reports, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot authorized examining a minority government with Ra'am inside and UTJ abstaining, possibly as leverage in unity talks; Yashar says such reports are not issued on its behalf. It falls short of 61 and Liberman rejects any government dependent on Arab or Haredi parties. Unnamed sources tell Ynet that Liberman berated Eisenkot at a Saturday meeting, saying the minority-government push hurt the bloc. On Nov 8 ANI, citing Haaretz and an unnamed senior Ra'am member, reported that Ra'am will support an Eisenkot government. A senior bloc figure told Ynet on Nov 8 that Liberman has no intention of backing a narrower emergency government without a majority. Eisenkot formally received the mandate on Nov 8 with 28 days to form a government, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 8 Liberman posted that he would not help establish a government dependent on Arab parties, Ynet reports. A Ynet analysis on Nov 8, citing people close to Eisenkot, says he sees unity with Netanyahu as a last resort and may bring a minority government to a confidence vote without full coalition agreement. On Nov 8 Golan said that if Liberman wants a government that won't draft the Haredim he can form one with Netanyahu, while Liberman called Golan's criticism stupid and malicious, Ynet reports. Ynet reports that at their Nov 9 meeting Liberman asked Eisenkot to drop the idea of a minority government backed by Arab parties. On Nov 10 Ynet reported, citing unnamed sources, that Abbas has agreed in principle to Eisenkot's condition of recognizing Hamas as a terrorist organization, and Golan confirmed talks with Ra'am are underway.

blockers.text: Liberman told Ynet that supporting a minority government would hand Netanyahu the premiership.
Ynet reports Bennett opposes any government reliant on Arab parties, expecting it to collapse.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Shas And UTJ
scenarios.note: No Arab parties needed, but the Haredi draft splits it. A source close to Eisenkot tells Ynet he is trying to bring Shas and UTJ into a government he leads, naming Liberman as the main obstacle. A senior UTJ official told Ynet the party would offer Eisenkot the premiership for draft exemptions, which clashes with his national-service condition; Shas is reported to be out. Unnamed senior UTJ figures say the party might back an Eisenkot government from outside without a draft law first, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 2 Liberman declined to rule out cooperating with UTJ, saying the bloc will have to see what happens. Ynet reports on Nov 3 that Eisenkot is focusing on courting the Haredi parties and that Liberman has left the door open to talks on including them. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 3 that Shas and UTJ stress no decision has been made, with their rabbis due back around the start of consultations. On Nov 4 Shas recommended Netanyahu, and Yisrael Beiteinu told Herzog it would not compromise key priorities to bring Haredi parties in, Ynet reports. On Nov 5 UTJ declined to recommend either candidate, with Goldknopf telling Herzog the party is not bound to any bloc, Ynet reports. ANI reports UTJ told Herzog its support for any government depends on legislation exempting yeshiva students from service. On Nov 5 Together told Herzog it will not accept a draft-evasion law, Israel National News reports. Channel 12 reports Liberman has dropped his refusal to sit with UTJ and that the opposition is in talks with it, but Yisrael Beiteinu told the Jerusalem Post it was not aware of this. Channel 12 reports the bloc is examining a coalition with UTJ and Shas, with draft talks starting from Liberman's 2018 bill, while Shas still stands with Likud. On Nov 6 Liberman said he is willing to be flexible and compromise on the Haredi draft law, the Jerusalem Post reports. The Times of Israel reports Liberman has confirmed he is open to a coalition with Haredi parties, reversing a key promise. After Liberman's shift, Eisenkot reiterated his demand for mandatory national service, the Times of Israel reports, and UTJ said it will back whoever solves the draft issue, Israel National News reports. UTJ leader Asher said on Nov 6 that no coalition proposal has yet been made to the party and that its rabbis will decide on any offer, the Times of Israel reports. Al Jazeera notes that adding UTJ and Shas would give Eisenkot a bare majority, as Herzog prepares to hand him the mandate. On Nov 7 Golan said he is open to a government with the Haredim on conditions including enlistment of young Haredim and no blank check, adding that they must come to meet his party in Ramat Gan. An unnamed Shas Council of Torah Sages source told Channel 12 that Shas would not act against UTJ's rabbis if they approve a deal, but Shas itself called reports it could join an Eisenkot government fake news, the Times of Israel reports. Ynet reports on Nov 8 that Likud's main pressure is on Deri, whom Likud officials expect, though not with certainty, to refuse the opposition; a senior bloc figure told Ynet the only option is the bloc plus the Haredi parties, or another election. Eisenkot formally received the mandate on Nov 8 with 28 days to form a government, the Jerusalem Post reports. On Nov 8 Liberman said he still backs military service for Haredi men while seeking understandings with the Haredi parties, Ynet reports. On Nov 9 the Jerusalem Post, citing unnamed UTJ sources, reports no agreement yet on joining Eisenkot, with conditions on Shabbat, kashrut, conversion and the religious status quo, and assessments that Shas would follow if UTJ joins first. Kikar HaShabbat reporter Yishai Cohen told 103FM that Shas could consider backing Eisenkot if yeshiva students' status is settled, but is waiting for UTJ to move first. On Nov 9 Ynet reported that Yashar invited Shas and UTJ to back a bid to replace Speaker Ohana at the Knesset's opening session; UTJ declined and Shas was not expected to join, while UTJ has not denied talks with the change bloc. On Nov 9 Kan reported that Eisenkot and Liberman agreed to open talks with Shas and UTJ, offering a softened draft law with a transition period, and Channel 12 said the talks were at an early stage, the Times of Israel reports. An unnamed senior UTJ source told JFeed a significant week lies ahead on cooperation with the change bloc, conditional on preserving the religious status quo. On Nov 10 Ynet reported, citing unnamed sources, that the bloc's parties intend first to try a government with the Haredi parties, and that Liberman has told Eisenkot he will bring them in. On Nov 10 UTJ leader Asher told Kikar HaShabbat the party won't join any coalition without draft exemptions, untouched Haredi school funding and the religion-state status quo, and Goldknopf told Channel 12 there have been preliminary contacts with Eisenkot's camp, the Times of Israel reports. The same day Shas said it still supports Netanyahu and is not in talks with any other player, the Times of Israel reports. Ynet reports Netanyahu met Asher on Nov 9 to keep UTJ from joining Eisenkot, and Asher gave no commitment. HNGN reports Asher said UTJ will not back replacing Speaker Ohana before a new government is formed. On Nov 11 the Jerusalem Post reported internal divisions within Eisenkot's bloc amid the Haredi coalition talks. A Jerusalem Post analysis on Nov 11 says Eisenkot chose Kahana over Lapid for Speaker, citing unnamed sources, and that the pick could strain ties with the Haredi parties. On Nov 12 the Times of Israel cited Channel 12 reporting that Rabbi Moshe Hillel Hirsch authorized UTJ to open talks with Eisenkot's bloc and that Asher met Liberman on Nov 11, with both sides saying no formal negotiations are underway; Hirsch himself said he doubts a deal is realistic, and Kan reports Moshe Gafni is working to block one. On Nov 12 Kan reported that senior UTJ figures have opened a regular channel with Ra'am and Joint List leaders to share updates on their talks with Eisenkot's bloc, while Asher's office called his conversations with Abbas and Tibi casual, JFeed reports. On Nov 12 Ynet reported, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot's bloc is weighing a one-year suspension of draft enforcement, including arrests, to win UTJ's support. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 13 that Eisenkot's camp wants UTJ in first with Ra'am abstaining and Shas later, that Liberman prefers Shas from the start, and that Deri has yet to decide. On Nov 13 the Times of Israel, citing Channel 12, reported that Agudat Yisrael's rabbinic advisers want every MK in Eisenkot's bloc to sign a pledge on a draft-exemption law with a court override clause. Ynet reports on Nov 13, citing unnamed bloc sources, that the preferred route is UTJ joining a minority government first, then Shas or Likud defectors, and that progress has been made with the Haredi parties. HNGN reports the bloc suspects Golan and Bennett are not committed to a coalition with the Haredi parties. The Jerusalem Post reports that on Nov 11 UTJ MKs Porush and Stark filed a bill freezing draft-evasion arrests and enforcement pending a yeshiva-student law, while Bennett filed a bill cutting support to households that neither serve nor work.

scenarios.name: National Unity Government
scenarios.note: The Jerusalem Post reports Netanyahu-linked sources are promoting it, possibly with a rotating premiership and without Shas and UTJ. Kan cites Netanyahu associate Benny Biton as saying Netanyahu wants unity, and an unnamed Likud official named Herzog and Trump as guarantors for Eisenkot. Channel 12 reports Liberman wants Eisenkot to join Netanyahu, though not under his own banner. Who would lead it is the sticking point. Likud whip Ofir Katz told Army Radio the party opposes rotation and others can join the existing coalition. Channel 14 reports, citing unnamed sources, that Netanyahu has given up on unity talks and is preparing for a new election. Ynet reports Netanyahu told associates privately he is not ruling out any option, including rotation, and that Katz says unity is off if the opposition ousts Speaker Ohana. On Nov 2 Netanyahu said publicly he is open to a broad government with any party that does not support terrorism but that he should lead it; an associate told Ynet no unity proposal has yet been made. Israel Hayom reports a Likud source's assessment, not a negotiated offer, that Netanyahu could accept unity if he served about two years and then became president, with Eisenkot taking over. ANI, citing the Times of Israel, reports Shas Council of Torah Sages member Rabbi Moshe Maya urged a unity government. On Nov 5 Yashar's delegation rejected a unity government with Netanyahu and called him the obstacle to unity, the Times of Israel reports. On Nov 5 Likud MK Yoav Kisch urged a broad national government and called on the opposition to end its boycott, the Times of Israel reports. After Herzog's decision on Nov 7, Netanyahu called in a video for a national unity government including all his current allies, which the Times of Israel calls a likely non-starter. Kan reports, citing an unnamed associate, that Netanyahu would discuss rotation if unity talks were held, and that an envoy's approach to Eisenkot was rebuffed; Yashar said it knew of no such approach and that Likud can join an Eisenkot-led coalition without extremists. Ynet reports on Nov 8 that Netanyahu is expected to pursue unity in the coming days, though unnamed senior Likud ministers had privately called it too costly and preferred another election; Yashar called his speech hysterical and said it would consider unity only if Likud breaks with its extremists. On receiving the mandate on Nov 8, Eisenkot appealed to Likud and Smotrich's party to join a government he would lead, AFP reports. The Jerusalem Post reports on Nov 9 that Netanyahu has launched an effort to block an Eisenkot government while still calling for unity, with disputes over who would lead it. In his Nov 10 Knesset speech Netanyahu again asked MKs to form a national unity government, and Eisenkot replied that the speech was hate-filled and Netanyahu unfit for office, urging a national emergency government instead, the Jerusalem Post reports. Yashar had announced a preliminary negotiating meeting with Likud for Nov 11, but Eisenkot cancelled it after Netanyahu's Nov 10 speech, while Likud said it would meet any faction seeking unity, the Jerusalem Post reports. Ynet reports on Nov 10 that the planned Likud–Yashar! meeting is cancelled, Likud has not formally set up a negotiating team, and contacts between Eisenkot envoy Ronen Manelis and Netanyahu's lawyer Michael Rabello are moving away from a deal. In his Nov 10 speech Netanyahu ruled out rotation and said a unity government must include all national-camp parties, including the Haredim, Ynet reports. Haaretz reports on Nov 11 that leaders of Eisenkot's bloc learned of the planned Yashar!–Likud talks only after they were cancelled. On Nov 11 Smotrich urged Netanyahu and Eisenkot to sit together and said understandings can be reached, Ynet reports. Ynet reported late on Nov 11, citing sources close to Netanyahu, that Likud would not insist on including Otzma Yehudit in a unity government; Likud denied it, saying Netanyahu called for unity based on the right-wing bloc's parties. Ynet reports on Nov 13, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot has told his team to resume talks with Likud next week, with unity seen as an option if Haredi talks stall.
